source_name: Banka Slovenije – Seznam notifikacij plačilnih institucij (passporting notifications, PDF/catalogue)
why_relevant: Codebook/catalogue for the list of inbound passporting notifications of foreign payment institutions into Slovenia — i.e. the foreign PSP population competing in SI without local licence. Complements the EBA PSD2 register with the national view.

source_name: UPPD – Smernice (guidelines PDF library on gov.si)
why_relevant: The Office's own guidelines for obliged entities (ocena tveganja PD/FT, sector guidelines). These define concrete control expectations and implementation deadlines for banks and payment institutions.

source_name: UPPD – Mnenja urada o dejanskih lastnikih (opinions library)
why_relevant: Compiled Office opinions on identifying beneficial owners — the practical interpretation banks must apply during customer due diligence; changes here move operational KYC requirements.

source_name: ZBS — news / obvestila on payment regulation implementation (Instant Payments Regulation, VoP)
why_relevant: ZBS publishes market-facing notices that state exactly when SI banks must have implemented scheme/regulatory changes (e.g. 9 October 2025 full instant-payment obligation and Verification of Payee, transitional period to 2027 for non-euro member states). These are the operational deadline announcements for the whole SI participant base.

source_name: ZBS – Mnenja IRPS (published mediator opinions, PDF series)
why_relevant: Actual anonymised opinions in consumer-vs-bank disputes (e.g. account debits, online fraud/abuse, loan repayment). Case-level detail on disputed practices — card fraud liability, unauthorised transactions, fees — months before any supervisory circular.

source_name: ATVP – Javni posveti / consultations announcements (ESMA draft documents)
why_relevant: ATVP relays ESMA public consultations to Slovenian market participants, usually with national response deadlines — a primary early-warning signal for upcoming obligations on banks providing investment services.

source_name: Bankart — Opis plačilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij (SL/EN, versioned PDF)
why_relevant: The closest public equivalent to a scheme/system rulebook: describes BIPS, BIPS IP (domestic SCT Inst), BIPS T (cross-border instant via TIPS) and SIMP-PS, participation eligibility, settlement and financial-risk arrangements. Republished under a dated filename, so version deltas expose operational and compliance changes for participants.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. — annual reports (Letno poročilo)
why_relevant: Operator annual reports narrate system launches, participant counts, volumes and forward project pipeline (e.g. BIPS IP go-live Feb 2019, Flik launch). Useful for reconstructing scheme timelines and for early sight of the next year's mandatory participant projects.

source_name: Bank/PSP published complaint & ADR terms (Splošni pogoji za opravljanje plačilnih storitev za potrošnike)
why_relevant: Every Slovenian bank must publish, in its consumer payment-services T&Cs, the internal complaint procedure and the ADR body it recognises as competent. Comparing these across banks reveals which institutions accept ZBS IRPS, deadlines they commit to, and drift after regulatory changes.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija — customer regulatory notices (bank-as-publisher)
why_relevant: Banks' own sl-language customer notices state concrete compliance dates and operational interpretations of EU rules (e.g. Uredba EU 2024/886 instant payments, VoP payee verification from 9 Oct 2025) earlier and more plainly than regulator texts. Verified example found.

source_name: Forbes Slovenija / N1 — banking regulatory and merger reporting
why_relevant: Business media surfaces bank disclosures that are otherwise buried in PDFs (merger effects, capital decisions, supervisory pressure) and often quotes management on regulatory-change impact — a discovery layer for which disclosures to pull.

source_name: Chambers Global Practice Guides — Banking & Finance: Slovenia
why_relevant: Annual SI chapter authored by a local firm: a structured, dated adviser summary of the SI banking/payments regulatory framework and pending reforms, and a reliable pointer to which firm currently owns this subject matter.

source_name: PwC Slovenija — DORA (Uredba o digitalni operativni odpornosti) advisory page
why_relevant: Slovenian-language practitioner explainer of DORA scope and application dates; typical of adviser content that dates obligations earlier and more plainly than the regulator.

entity_name: SI bank participant disclosures of scheme obligations
source_name: SI bank participant disclosures of scheme obligations (Flik / IPR general terms and notices)
why_relevant: Individual SI banks publish the participant-facing version of scheme rules — Flik general terms, IPR implementation notices, changed cut-off times. Because the Flik rulebook itself is not public, aggregating several banks' 'splošni pogoji' is the practical proxy for reconstructing scheme requirements and their effective dates.

source_name: Banka Sparkasse d.d. — instant payments / payment services product pages
why_relevant: Steiermärkische-owned Slovenian bank; product pages document how the Instant Payments Regulation (9 Oct 2025) and Verification of Payee obligations were implemented commercially. Useful comparative datapoint against NLB/OTP.

source_name: Deloitte Slovenija — Financial Services (Finančne novičke) article series
why_relevant: Deloitte SI runs a Slovenian-language financial-services newsletter ('Finančne novičke') covering EU fintech/regulatory action plans and non-financial risk in financial institutions — exactly the adviser-translated regulation this cell targets. Recency of the series needs checking (located examples are older).

source_name: Incrementum d.o.o. – SI CASP authorisation announcements
why_relevant: One of the few SI firms holding an ATVP MiCA CASP authorisation; company announcements date the licence and describe permitted services — useful primary-firm evidence and a template for tracking the other SI CASPs.

source_name: iVarnost.si — DORA explainer for the financial sector
why_relevant: Non-law SI consultancy/media outlet producing sl-language DORA compliance commentary; useful as a cross-check on how SI practitioner audiences are being told to read ICT-resilience deadlines, and as a snowball into the SI cyber/compliance advisory community.

source_name: Konsentus – analysis of the EBA registers (data-quality commentary)
why_relevant: Vendor analysis documenting known inconsistencies, lag and duplication in the EBA PSD2 register and national registers. Useful as methodological guidance on how far to trust register-derived counts for SI, and it flags that national registers (like bsi.si) remain the legal source of truth.

source_name: Microsoft Trust Center - DORA compliance (Slovenian localisation)
why_relevant: Hyperscalers are DORA-designated ICT third-party providers to SI banks. Their sl-SI compliance pages and contractual addenda document exactly which DORA articles they cover for financial-entity customers - the supplier-side evidence of cloud dependency at private SI banks.

source_name: NLB Pillar 3 disclosures (Razkritja po 3. stebru baselskih standardov)
why_relevant: Annual and semi-annual CRR Part Eight disclosures containing TSCR/P2R/P2G levels, buffer requirements, MREL, and narrative on incoming regulatory change (CRR3/CRD6, DORA, ESG risk). Machine-comparable across years.

source_name: Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije (OZS) – IRPS / consumer-law guidance
why_relevant: Trade-chamber explainers on ADR obligations and consumer-law drafts, written for obliged traders. Shows how the obligation is understood/implemented on the business side and flags draft amendments early.

source_name: Open Banking Europe / PRETA – PSD2 registration & passporting guide
why_relevant: Explains how PSD2 registration and passporting entries are structured across national registers and the EBA register — the interpretation key for reading SI passporting entries correctly (host-state vs home-state, service codes).

source_name: OTP Group Slovenia annual report 2024 (third-party mirror)
why_relevant: Mirrors of bank annual reports on third-party sites (sustainability/media portals) provide fallback access when bank sites reorganise their opaque fileid-based download URLs. Confirms the 2024 report restates 2023 as if NKBM and SKB had operated combined.

source_name: SKB banka legacy report archive (within OTP banka site)
why_relevant: SKB merged into OTP banka on 2 Sept 2024 (legal merger 22 Aug 2024). Historic SKB annual reports and disclosures remain the baseline for pre-merger regulatory/compliance positions; archive now mirrored under otpbanka.si. skb.si itself is being wound down — capture before link rot.

source_name: Temenos Success Stories / Customer References (Nova Ljubljanska Banka)
why_relevant: Core-banking vendor reference page documenting NLB's T24/Transact deployment and later retail migration. Establishes which core platform the largest SI bank runs, which in turn determines the vendor channel through which regulatory change (IFRS, PSD2, DORA, instant payments) is delivered.

source_name: Tricikel d.o.o. - DORA / ICT risk consultancy content (sl)
why_relevant: Domestic ICT/GRC consultancy publishing Slovenian-language DORA explainers aimed at financial entities and their ICT suppliers. Local consultancies name the concrete national interplay (e.g. ZInfV-1) that global vendors omit.

source_name: UniCredit Developer Portal — Slovenia PSD2/instant-payments API newsroom
why_relevant: Bank developer portals reveal PSD2/instant-payments compliance timing at a technical level (sandbox availability, API version deadlines) months before customer-facing notices — an early-warning channel for payment regulation implementation in SI.

entity_name: ZMOS / interest-association consultation responses on payment-means law
source_name: ZMOS / interest-association consultation responses on payment-means law
why_relevant: Shows the non-bank stakeholder response channel and internal deadlines for the July 2026 draft Act on accessibility and use of payment means (cash right, free basic payment package) — a payments-policy file with direct implications for fintech and card acceptance.
